title: G. Traceability and maintenance
definition: Every card can be traced to the source units it represents; source-unit ids and semantic ids are stable across wording changes; source updates are reconciled correctly; user edits are preserved; ambiguous matches go to review.
questions: Can a note be traced back to its source?
Are source-unit IDs and semantic IDs stable?
Are source updates reconciled correctly (unchanged untouched, edited updated, new added, removed proposed)?
Are ambiguous matches routed to review?

severity.critical: A user edit overwritten; a card bound to the wrong passage; a removal applied silently; a card citing a unit it doesn't represent.
severity.major: An unchanged card regenerated (unnecessary churn); a renamed heading creating new identities.
severity.minor: A citation to a neighbouring unit that also supports the card.

deterministic: element_present for evidence elements (paths, line ranges)
future: cites on every card (ai.cites), unit lineage (reconcile.card-level)
model_judge: 'Does each cited passage support its card?' (offline)
human: Reviewer spot-checks citations and the update outcome

requiredAssertions: A future citation assertion per case
reconcile_state for the user-edited item in update cases (critical)
passCriteria: User edits survive every update; reconcile states match; once citations exist, every card's citations resolve to supporting units.
failCriteria: Any user edit lost, any silent removal, any wrong binding.
passExample: v2 rewords one paragraph: only the card citing it is updated; the user's edited card comes back as a conflict with 'Keep mine'.
failExample: v2 rewords one paragraph: the whole section is regenerated and the user's note is replaced by the new wording.

judgeScale.meaning: Every card traceable to its units; only what changed changes; edits always kept.
